summary: Cold-renderer blank grid, 10-15s. Measure before touching. Do not fix by reverting MPI-394. Not caused by MPI-396 (routes/ only).

Settings reported slow too (disk bar late, Disconnect locked). Settings is not an MpiTileSheet consumer, so a tile cause cannot explain it - added the remote-latency hypothesis and a cheap discriminator: open the library cold while DISCONNECTED. If fast, this merges into MPI-397 and the tile bisect is wasted work.

Discriminator run by the user: everything is fast LOCALLY, so this is remote latency/volume, not a renderer bug - tile bisect cancelled before any code was written. Reframed around MPI-326, whose storm fix gated the models:checked EMIT but not the ~5s heartbeat REQUEST RATE. Measure requests-per-minute first.

Implementation started - measurement only. Temp probe routes/_probe398.js counts local route hits and wraps globalThis.fetch to time every outbound wrapper call, so volume and latency come from one sample. Pod was NOT connected at move time (GET /remote/mode active:false), so the probe lands before the connect (routes/ is main-process = full restart).

MEASURED on a live CPU Pod (1fb5wwvnf2d9es, EU-RO-1, 150GB volume). ROOT CAUSE PROVEN with a negative control: /wrapper/disk runs du -sb /workspace as a bare subprocess.run inside an async handler (wrapper.py:750), blocking the wrapper's single asyncio loop for ~1.8s per call. models/check measured 0.19-0.64s alone, 1.37s and 0.98s while a du was in flight, then 0.18s the instant the du returned - ~7x inflation, collapsing back on cue. It fires 6.8/min at idle, so the wrapper is stalled ~20% of idle wall-clock; worst observed victim was /wrapper/stats (94ms p50) at 3576ms. This is MPI-191's asyncio.to_thread fix applied to one endpoint instead of the class - /wrapper/disk was written later for MPI-169 and kept the blocking call. TWO HYPOTHESES KILLED BY MEASUREMENT: (1) the card's prime lead is wrong - POST /wrapper/models/status fired ZERO times in 62s of idle, so MPI-326's storm has not regressed and is not the idle cost; (2) the per-dep stat theory is dead - a 1-dep and a 100-dep models/status cost the same (0.18-0.39s), so EU-RO-1 RTT is the floor and stat count is irrelevant. Idle total is ~59 outbound req/min (~1/s doing nothing), ~30% of wall-clock in flight, with paired inter-arrival gaps (0.06s inside a 6s cadence) suggesting duplicate pollers on /wrapper/stats and /wrapper/disk. NOT yet attributed: the 10-15s cold-renderer blank grid - needs a window reset immediately before a Ctrl+R. No fix written; it spans the Pod runtime and the app poll cadence, so it goes to the user as a brief first.

FIXED AT THE SOURCE and verified live four ways. wrapper.py /wrapper/disk: du now runs via asyncio.to_thread (MPI-191's fix applied to the endpoint it missed), behind an asyncio.Lock with a cache re-check INSIDE the lock so N concurrent callers cause ONE walk, plus a 60s TTL cache invalidated by _manifest_record_model (single choke point for all three install-complete paths) and models_delete - so the disk bar still drops instantly after an uninstall. Wrapper 0.2.38 -> 0.2.39, published to the R2 dev channel, confirmed live via wrapperVersion. App-side floor pin left at 0.2.36 on purpose (perf fix, not protocol). Client poll cadence deliberately untouched - the TTL makes it irrelevant and changing both would muddy attribution. PROOFS: (a) models/check during a real du 0.45-0.87s vs 0.51-0.96s alone, indistinguishable, where pre-fix it was 0.18s vs 1.37s; (b) a genuine 1759ms walk landed inside an idle window and /health maxed 513ms, /wrapper/stats 314ms, against 3576ms pre-fix; (c) 8 simultaneous disk calls all returned 200 within 240ms of each other on one shared walk, where pre-fix that shape gave 32s p50 and a 125s Cloudflare 524; (d) focused idle, same 6.5/min poll rate, disk p50 590->194ms and max 4241->258ms. CLASS SWEPT: /wrapper/ls has the same blocking pattern and is worse but has ZERO consumers, left alone deliberately. DOC DEFECT FIXED in mpi-ci: README and publish-runtime.sh both said step 3 of a wrapper edit is POST /wrapper/restart-comfy - it is not, that handler restarts only the ComfyUI subprocess and 409s on a download Pod, so only a Pod re-bootstrap loads new wrapper bytes; both now say re-bootstrap and VERIFY wrapperVersion, because a publish plus a no-op restart reads exactly like a failed fix. MEASUREMENT TRAP RECORDED: Chromium clamps a backgrounded window's setInterval to ~1/min, so podDiskBar's 10s poll reads 6.8/min focused and 0.9/min behind a terminal - two post-fix samples were nearly banked as a false improvement before this was caught; the client was never changed, so a poll-rate drop could not have been the fix. STILL OPEN: the cold-renderer blank grid, the one user-facing acceptance item. Three timed windows were opened for a Ctrl+R and the reload landed in none of them, proven by the absence of the boot markers the pre-fix cold-open sample carried. Probe stays mounted until that lands. Do NOT close this card on the four proofs alone.

SECOND OFFENDER found and fixed - wrapper 0.2.40. After 0.2.39 the user reported the Model Library opened really fast, but the probe disagreed and the probe was right: POST /wrapper/models/status min 2248ms p50 9942ms, with /wrapper/stats dragged to 8693ms and /health to 5014ms+ERR in the same window, while /wrapper/disk was already healthy at p50 310ms. The starvation signature had moved to a second synchronous on-loop handler. THIS SESSION'S OWN EARLIER MEASUREMENT HAD CLEARED IT WRONGLY: the 1-vs-100-dep sweep used absent filenames in a SINGLE checkpoints/ directory - negative lookups against one warm dentry cache - read 0.18-0.39s flat, and concluded stat count was irrelevant. Re-measured with 86 REAL filenames across their real subdirs: 2.06s/2.24s/0.66s real vs 0.99s/1.09s/0.64s absent, i.e. ~2x for real paths and ~5x the synthetic figure, warming after the first pass. A synthetic profile of absent files in one directory understates this endpoint by about an order of magnitude. Fix: the whole per-model scan moved into asyncio.to_thread, NOT cached on purpose since install-state feeds the entire download UI and must stay truthful. PROOF on a FRESH Pod (the user's Disconnect deleted rather than stopped it, so nothing was cached - the harshest case): real 86-dep check 1.947s/0.948s/0.572s, and /remote/pod/stats measured 0.092/0.097/0.063/0.060s WHILE two real checks ran concurrently, against 8693ms for that same shape pre-fix. Probe over the window: models/status max 1264ms, /wrapper/stats max 94ms. Both offenders now off the loop, each proven by the same negative control - run the expensive thing, watch whether a cheap neighbour notices. PROCESS NOTE: this card was nearly closed twice on bad evidence, once on a poll-rate drop that was really Chromium throttling a backgrounded window, once on a subjective 'really fast' that coincided with a 9942ms call still in the log. Keep the instrument mounted until the last acceptance item is measured.

USER-VERIFIED on a FRESH Pod, cold renderer and cold volume metadata - user's words: it was instant, against the reported 10-15s blank grid. Reload confirmed PRESENT in the sample rather than assumed (/project-file x32, models/check x5, get-path, list-projects, version-check, deps-status - the boot markers three earlier false-start windows lacked). Cold-open before -> after: /health p50 5013ms with 3 of 4 ERR -> p50 141ms, 30/30 OK; /wrapper/manifest p50 13714ms -> 282ms; /wrapper/disk p50 32294ms max 125072ms+524 -> p50 371ms; models/status p50 8679ms -> p50 2259ms. KNOWN CEILING STATED, NOT BURIED: models/status still peaks at 7774ms and disk at 4863ms on a fresh Pod - genuine first-touch cost on cold network-volume metadata (min 92ms / 65ms once warm, so one-time per boot). What changed is that they starve nothing: /wrapper/stats held 512ms max and /health 357ms max straight through them, all 200s. Caching install-state the way disk now caches du is the known next step and was deliberately NOT done - that cache sits under the whole download UI and correctness beats one cold scan per boot. Uncarded on purpose. NOT PROMOTED: dev is 0.2.40, stable is 0.2.38, and mpi-release owns that gate (never auto-promote, same class as git push) - the user identified this correctly mid-session. Probe fully reverted, server.js diff empty. Changelog entry added to UNRELEASED.md fixes. Card sits doing/validating pending the user's explicit go to close.
